qualityBar.verdict: A large, earnest JRPG where the party shares its growth and even a defensive turn changes the reward you bring home.

set.longDescription:
Theia: The Crimson Eclipse begins with a world running short of the resource that built it. Ariathale's Atlas mineral powered technology for years, and the rush to use it left a crisis behind. Its leaders ban that technology while they look for another answer. Seth, a former imperial guard, becomes a person of interest to the people who think he knows where an answer might be. He would rather keep moving. That chase gives a long, character-heavy adventure its first push.

MissingSeven made Theia as a free, non-commercial RPG Maker 2003 game. Its itch.io page describes a large cast of nineteen playable characters, a story with multiple endings, side quests and a main path measured in dozens of hours. Those are the creator's figures, not a promise about any player's pace. The interesting detail is how the cast changes. Some companions arrive as guests, unable to change weapons or learn skills until their story gives them a reason to stay. Party membership becomes more than a number on a roster.

Combat has several overlapping decisions. Non-guest members share a pool of Ability Points for unlocking skills, so building one character means deciding what to delay for another. Craftable weapons can hold Atlas Shards for bonuses, and particular pairings unlock extra synergies. Each character also has an Exceed technique, charged through a particular battle command. On top of that, aggressive actions fill a Mastery Bar that improves post-battle rewards, while defending and item use drain it. Sometimes the safe move keeps the party alive but gives back the bonus you were building. The camp menu lets you talk to companions and change what they bring to the road ahead.

The creator lists the download for Windows and documents keyboard input. There is no browser version behind the old PlayBound listing, no published Mac or Linux build, and no native-controller layout that we can claim. There is no multiplayer mode or dedicated server to connect a party to. The English version is a 548 MB RAR download from the creator's itch.io page; the other large archives are language variants. Download one language, extract it, then run its executable. Numerical hardware requirements are not published.

The creator also warns that this non-commercial game uses some assets made for other works. PlayBound links to the creator's own download and does not mirror or redistribute those files while the rights are unclear. We want to test the full installation and combat pacing before deciding whether it clears our quality bar. Even as a Draft, Theia deserves an accurate description: it is a substantial single-player JRPG, and its shared growth systems give every new companion an immediate cost and possibility.
set.whyWePickedIt: Theia's shared Ability Points, conditional party membership and Mastery Bar give its long JRPG campaign more to think about than simply choosing the next attack. We are keeping it in Draft while checking the download, play quality and third-party asset rights.
set.thatOneThing: Defending can drain the reward meter you built by attacking; surviving the fight may cost you the good loot.

installSteps.text: Open MissingSeven's official Theia page on itch.io and download the English Orihalcon V2-08 RAR, or choose one of the other language archives. The archives are language variants of the same game.
Extract the entire RAR archive with an archive utility. Run the game executable inside the extracted folder; the creator does not provide a browser version.
Use a keyboard. The optional Fast Message Patch is separate and should be installed only if you want its Shift-to-display-message behavior.

firstPlaySteps.text: In the first battles, check which characters are guests before spending shared Ability Points or planning a weapon upgrade.
Watch the Mastery Bar as you attack, defend and use items; those choices change your post-battle bonuses.

faq.q: Can I play Theia in a browser?
faq.a: No. The creator publishes downloadable Windows RAR archives, not a browser edition.
Yes. MissingSeven distributes it as a free, non-commercial game. The creator warns that some assets belong to other rights holders, so PlayBound does not redistribute the archive.
The English Orihalcon V2-08 archive is listed at 548 MB compressed on the creator's itch.io page. Installed size is not verified.

faq.q: Does it support controllers or multiplayer?
faq.a: The creator documents keyboard input and a single-player RPG. No native-controller layout, PlayBound Controls profile, multiplayer mode or dedicated server has been verified.
Yes. The itch.io page lists English, Italian, German and Spanish archives; the creator says they are otherwise the same game.
